output.brief:
Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump comes from the 2 Nov storage compaction tuning change (FC-7710), not gateway 5.8. That change raised compaction threads from 2 to 6 and pushed disks from about 41% to 97% busy. Read queue waits rose from 9 ms to 205 ms, and node-side GET time from 61 ms to 262 ms.

Two things show the gateway isn't the cause. Latency rose in each cell within minutes of the config push, regardless of when 5.8 reached that cell. One cell, aps-3, got 5.8 but skipped the push, and its latency stayed at about 94 ms. A rollback test in euw-1 changed nothing.

Network and traffic growth don't explain it. A rollback would also reopen the security hole for no latency gain.

Next step: revert the tuning in one cell first, and watch GET p99 and compaction backlog. If p99 drops and backlog stays below 15%, extend the revert to the other cells. aps-3 is a natural comparison cell. Don't pause compaction, because backlog would grow and disks could fill. Hold off on rate-limiting Orrin until the 10 Nov backlog attribution shows what's driving backlog. Keep 5.8 on track for the 30 Nov audit deadline. Confidence is high.
